subtitle: A hunted heir carves a kingdom from a matrilineal coast

panels.shot: dramatic low-angle mid-shot in monsoon dusk
panels.action: Young Marthanda Varma stands on a rain-slick laterite rampart, bare-chested under a white upper cloth, hand resting on a sheathed sword, lightning splitting the sky over palm-fringed backwaters behind him.

dialogue.text: In a small coastal land where kingship passed through women, a boy named Marthanda Varma lived each day knowing his cousins and nobles were already planning his death.

i18n.hi: एक छोटे तटीय देस में, जहाँ राजगद्दी औरतों से चलती थी, मार्तांड वर्मा नाम का लड़का रोज़ जीता था ये जानते हुए कि उसके चचेरे और सरदार पहले ही उसकी मौत की साज़िश बुन रहे हैं।

panels.shot: wide aerial over Kerala coast at sunrise
panels.action: The camera floats over a strip of land between the Arabian Sea and the Western Ghats, dotted with lagoons, coconut groves, tiled-roof houses and temple towers, as morning mist coils over the backwaters.

dialogue.text: Early eighteenth-century Venad was a narrow coast of lagoons and laterite, but its politics were wider than the sea: Dutch forts, English factors, Brahmin councils and warrior chiefs all tugged at a fragile crown.

i18n.hi: अठारहवीं सदी की शुरुआत वाला वेनाड तंग सा लैटराइट‑तटीय पट्टा था, पर उसकी सियासत समंदर से भी चौड़ी: डच किले, अंग्रेज फैक्टर, ब्राह्मण सभाएँ और वीर नायक — सब एक नाज़ुक ताज को खींच रहे थे।

panels.shot: slow push-in on Attingal palace courtyard
panels.action: Inside the Attingal palace, women in white and gold saris sit on a raised verandah, while young boys play in the courtyard; a matriarchal figure watches, finger counting genealogies on a palm-leaf manuscript.

dialogue.text: Here, in the royal house of Attingal, power followed marumakkathayam: succession through sisters and their children, so that a queen’s son, not a king’s, would inherit Venad.

i18n.hi: यहीं अट्टिंगल के राजमहल में सत्ता चलती थी मरुमक्कथेयम से: उतराधिकार बहनों और उनके बच्चों से, ताकि राजा नहीं, रानी का बेटा वेनाड का वारिस बने।

panels.action: A toddler Marthanda Varma sits on the lap of Queen Karthika Thirunal Umadevi, who traces his cheek with affection; a Kilimanoor prince stands respectfully nearby, shadows of palace pillars framing them.

dialogue.text: In 1706, Karthika Thirunal Umadevi of Attingal bore a son by Raghava Varma of Kilimanoor. By the law of the land, this child, Marthanda Varma, stood in the line to the Venad throne.

i18n.hi: १७०६ में अट्टिंगल की कार्तिका तिरुनाल उमादेवी ने किलिमनूर के राघव वर्मा से एक पुत्र जना। देश के नियम से यही बालक, मार्तांड वर्मा, वेनाड की गद्दी की पंक्ति में खड़ा था।

panels.action: On one side of the frame, palace women point to a matrilineal family tree painted on the wall; on the other, stern male cousins stand around a palm-leaf deed showing their patrilineal line, faces tight with resolve.

dialogue.text: But cousins like Valiya Thampi and Kunju Thampi claimed by a different logic: they were sons of Venad princes. They argued that a man’s bloodline, not a sister’s womb, should decide the next king.

i18n.hi: मगर वालेय थम्पि और कुंजु थम्पि जैसे चचेरे और तर्क लाते थे: वे वेनाड के राजकुमारों के बेटे थे। उनका कहना था कि राज तय करे आदमी की नस्ल, बहन की कोख नहीं।

panels.shot: dim interior wide-shot of council hall
panels.action: A hall lit by oil lamps where Nair chieftains, Brahmin elders and palace officials sit in tense rows; a scroll bearing the words of an old grant lies on a low desk, untouched, as hands gesture in heated debate.

dialogue.text: Nagam Aiya and old court records speak of these quarrels: nobles of Venad weighing marumakkathayam custom against the ambitions of powerful Thampis, while Dutch merchants and rival houses watched from the wings.

i18n.hi: नागम अय्यर और पुराने दरबारी रजिस्टर इन झगड़ों का ज़िक्र करते हैं: वेनाड के सरदार मरुमक्कथेयम रिवाज़ तोल रहे थे ताकतवर थम्पियों की हसरतों के सामने, जबकि डच सौदागर और प्रतिद्वंदी घराने किनारे से तमाशा देख रहे थे।

panels.shot: low-angle courtyard wide with child at center
panels.action: A slightly older Marthanda Varma practices with a wooden stick in a dusty courtyard, sweat on his brow; in the shaded colonnade, shadowy figures whisper, one hand slicing across the throat in a silent gesture.

dialogue.text: While the law seemed clear, power was not. Court tradition, preserved by Shungoonny Menon, remembers whispers in corridors: that the boy marked by law would be cut down before he could wear the crown.

i18n.hi: कानून साफ दिखता था, पर ताकत धुंधली। शुंगुन्नि मेनन ने बचाई दरबारी परंपरा में गलियारों की फुसफुसाहटें हैं: कि जो लड़का क़ानून से चुना गया है, उसे ताज छूने से पहले ही काट गिराया जाएगा।

panels.shot: nighttime overhead shot in a small room
panels.action: By the light of a single oil lamp, young Marthanda Varma lies awake on a simple mat, eyes open and alert, as a faint silhouette darkens the lattice window behind him, dagger glinting in moonlight.

dialogue.text: Menon’s nineteenth-century history records many escapes—later retold with awe. Whether each detail can be proved or not, it is clear from the record that attempts on his life shadowed his youth.

i18n.hi: मेनन की उन्नीसवीं सदी की इतिहास‑किताब उसके कई फ़रार गिनाती है — बाद में जिनका ज़िक्र दंग होकर हुआ। हर बात साबित हो या न हो, रिकॉर्ड साफ कहता है कि उसकी जवानी पर जानलेवा साये लगे रहे।

panels.shot: dynamic mid-shot at a riverside ghat
panels.action: Marthanda Varma, now a teenager, wades hurriedly through a shallow river at dawn with his cloth hitched, looking back over his shoulder, while distant riders on the bank search, their silhouettes small but threatening.

dialogue.text: One strand of court memory places him hiding near Budhanoor, slipping through temple courtyards and along river banks, moving from house to house whenever word came that Thampi partisans were near.

i18n.hi: दरबार की एक याद उसे बुधनूर के पास छुपा बताती है — मंदिर प्रांगणों से फिसलते, नदी किनारों से गुजरते, और थम्पि के लोग पास दिखें तो घर से घर बदलते।

panels.action: In a modest Brahmin house, Marthanda Varma sits cross-legged on a mat, hands folded, as an elderly householder in simple white speaks to him, a lamp between them casting long shadows on the wall.

dialogue.text: “Princes come and go, child. Dharma must stand,” the elder says softly.

i18n.hi: “राजकुमार आते‑जाते हैं, बच्चा। धरम टिकना चाहिए,” बूढ़ा हल्के से कहता है।

panels.action: A close profile of Marthanda Varma lit by the flicker of the lamp, his features set in concentration as voices drift from another room, hinting at discussions of law, temples and succession.

dialogue.text: Menon notes that sympathisers sheltered him, some from devotion to the Attingal line, some from loyalty to temple trusts intertwined with that line. In hiding, the prince listened and learned what bound this land.

i18n.hi: मेनन लिखता है कि हमदर्दों ने उसे पनाह दी — कुछ अट्टिंगल वंश के प्रति भक्ति से, कुछ उन मंदिर ट्रस्टों से निष्ठा से जो उसी वंश में गुंथे थे। छिपते‑छिपते राजकुमार सुनता रहा, और सीखा कि ये धरती किस डोर से बंधी है।

panels.action: A composite panel: a temple courtyard in Budhanoor, a grove near Nagercoil, a village lane by Kalkulam fort, each with a fleeting figure of the prince blending into the crowd as different households discreetly aid him.

dialogue.text: From Attingal to Budhanoor, from Nagercoil to Kalkulam, the story repeats: a hunted heir relying on scattered allies—Kilimanoor kin, loyal Nairs, temple circles—to stay one step ahead of those who saw him as an obstacle.

i18n.hi: अट्टिंगल से बुधनूर, नागरकोइल से कल्कुलम तक वही दास्तान दोहरती है: शिकार बना वारिस, बिखरे साथियों पर टिका — किलिमनूर के रिश्तेदार, वफ़ादार नायर, मंदिर के घेरे — ताकि जो उसे रुकावट समझते थे, उनसे एक कदम आगे रहे।

panels.action: Inside a sanctum-like hall, priests and nobles prepare for an elaborate rite; a golden pot and sacred fire dominate the foreground, while a young prince watches from behind a carved pillar, half-hidden.

dialogue.text: The kingdom’s own records speak of royal-sacral rites, like hiranyagarbha-like ceremonies, used to sacralise authority and claim ancient roots. Such rituals proclaimed divine sanction, whatever the actual lineage debates.

i18n.hi: राज्य के अपने रिकॉर्ड राज‑धार्मिक कर्मकांडों का ज़िक्र करते हैं, हिरण्यगर्भ जैसे विधान, जिनसे राजसत्ता पवित्र बनती और खुद को प्राचीन जड़ों से जोड़ती। ऐसी रस्में दैवी मंज़ूरी का ऐलान करतीं, चाहे असल वंशवाद की बहस कुछ भी हो।

panels.shot: medium shot of legal instruction scene
panels.action: Marthanda Varma sits on a low bench in a shaded verandah as a learned Brahmin unrolls a palm-leaf manuscript, pointing to lines while the young prince watches closely, jaw clenched in determination.

dialogue.text: Meanwhile, the legal frame hardened. The marumakkathayam principle, later echoed even in modern court judgments on temple and royal disputes, confirmed the Attingal line’s rights over Venad’s throne and treasures.

i18n.hi: उधर क़ानूनी ढांचा सख्त हुआ। मरुमक्कथेयम सिद्धांत, जिसे बाद में मंदिर और राज‑विवादों पर आधुनिक अदालतों ने भी दोहराया, अट्टिंगल वंश का वेनाड की गद्दी और ख़ज़ानों पर हक़ पक्का करता रहा।

panels.action: In a packed council hall, opposing factions face each other: on one side, supporters of the Attingal line; on the other, stern Thampi allies, hands on sword-hilts, while a central elder raises his hand for silence.

dialogue.text: Yet law did not silence resentment. The Thampis and their noble allies, described in both Menon and the Travancore Manual, continued to challenge, turning every drought, every tax, every slight into fresh grievance.

i18n.hi: पर कानून ने कुढ़न नहीं दबाई। थम्पि और उनके सामंती साथी, जिनका ज़िक्र मेनन और ट्रावणकोर मैनुअल दोनों में है, चुनौती देते रहे — हर सूखे, हर लगान, हर बेइज़्ज़ती को नई शिकायत में बदलते हुए।

panels.shot: intense mid-shot outside a temple at twilight
panels.action: At twilight before a temple, Marthanda Varma stands alone beneath a banyan tree, hands clasped, looking at the tower; villagers pass in the background, some nodding in respect, others watching warily.

dialogue.text: “If I live, this land must be more than a prize,” he thinks.

i18n.hi: “अगर मैं जिंदा रहूँ, तो ये धरती सिर्फ़ इनाम नहीं रहेगी,” वह मन ही मन सोचता है।

panels.shot: commanding low-angle shot in palace courtyard
panels.action: Marthanda Varma, now a young man, stands upright in a palace courtyard, flanked by a few loyal Nairs; beyond them, stoic courtiers bow slightly, acknowledging his position without warmth, tension palpable.

dialogue.text: By the late 1720s, the hunted youth had become the accepted heir in practice, though not yet the unchallenged ruler. Every bow he received in Kalkulam or Attingal carried both reluctant obedience and unspoken threat.

i18n.hi: १७२० के आख़िर तक, वो शिकार बना नौजवान अमल में तो मान्य वारिस बन चुका था, पर अभी सर्वमान्य शासक नहीं। कल्कुलम हो या अट्टिंगल, हर प्रणाम में आधा‑अधूरा सिर झुकना था, आधा‑छिपा खतरा भी।

panels.shot: close-up on face, half in light, half in shadow
panels.action: A tight close-up of Marthanda Varma’s face, one side lit by sunlight from a palace window, the other in shadow; outside, faintly visible, soldiers drill in formation within the fort walls.

dialogue.text: The prince who would not die had learned from each narrow escape: law mattered, ritual mattered, allies mattered—yet none of them alone could hold Venad together in an age of factions and foreign guns.

i18n.hi: जो राजकुमार मरने को तैयार नहीं हुआ, उसने हर तंग बचाव से सीखा: कानून ज़रूरी है, रस्में ज़रूरी हैं, साथी ज़रूरी हैं — पर इनमें से कोई अकेला वेनाड को बचा नहीं सकता था, गुटों और विदेशी तोपों के इस दौर में।

panels.shot: epic wide shot of coast and fortress in background
panels.action: From a fort balcony overlooking the sea, Marthanda Varma gazes toward the line of the horizon where a European ship sails, while behind him the tiled roofs, temples and fields of Venad stretch inland.

dialogue.text: Survival had given him time; the matrilineal law had given him a claim. What he would now build from that fragile advantage—a new Travancore carved from this small coast—would decide why his name endured.

i18n.hi: बचने ने उसे वक़्त दिया; मातृसत्तात्मक कानून ने उसे दावा। अब वो इसी नाज़ुक बढ़त से क्या गढ़ेगा — इस छोटे तट से काटा हुआ नया त्रावणकोर — यही तय करेगा कि उसका नाम क्यों सदियों तक गूंजा।

title_i18n.en: The Prince Who Would Not Die
title_i18n.hi: जो राजकुमार मरने से इनकार करता था

subtitle_i18n.en: A hunted heir carves a kingdom from a matrilineal coast
subtitle_i18n.hi: शिकार बना वारिस, मातृसत्तात्मक तट से गढ़ता है राज्य
